title: GLSL lowering: shaders/CultMath.glsl is generated from CultMath.hlsl by one enumerated textual transformation, pinned by a test, compiled by glslang, with a committed golden fixture for WebGL2 parity
first: Map: docs/cultmath-interval-ground-cut.md, sections 'Where the interval math lives' (route C) and 'The authority map'. Model: the HLSL -> C# mirror in tests/CultMath.Tests/HlslSourceCompatibilityTests.cs (wrapper at :348) and its complete transformation list in packages/cultmath/docs/design.md:92-134. The GLSL lowering follows the same discipline: a complete, enumerated list; anything outside it fails the test rather than being patched around.
Read how HlslSourceCompatibilityTests resolves #include "CultMath.Phacelle.hlsl" (CultMath.hlsl:506); the GLSL lowering inlines the included file at that line, because GLSL has no #include.

Target dialect: GLSL ES 3.00 (#version 300 es), WebGL2. No implicit int/uint -> float conversion; step(vec4, float) and max(vec4, float) differ (max(genType, float) exists, step(genType, float) does not); C-style casts do not exist; lerp/frac/saturate/rsqrt/asuint are mix/fract/clamp(x,0.0,1.0)/inversesqrt/floatBitsToUint; floatN/intN are vecN/ivecN; static const is const. Mixed-signedness shifts are allowed.

Where the lowered text does not compile, fix the HLSL into the common subset with a legal, bit-identical HLSL edit (e.g. CultMath.hlsl:114 and :200 step(h, 0.0) -> step(h, float4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)); :471-473 and :502 (float)((uint)hash.x >> 8) before the float multiply). The HLSL -> C# mirror test and the FXC/dxc compiles keep those edits honest. Never special-case the lowering for one function.
Casts need a balanced-paren scanner, not a regex: (int)((state >> 28) + 4) at CultMath.hlsl:396 is the case that breaks a regex.

Dropped, as the C# mirror drops them: include guards (replaced by CULTMATH_GLSL guards), and the Texture2D/SamplerState functions at CultMath.hlsl:535-573. The GLSL declares no precision; the host shader does (precision highp float; precision highp int; the pcg hashes need 32-bit int).
Regeneration: the pin test writes shaders/CultMath.glsl when the environment variable CULTMATH_WRITE_GLSL=1 is set, then asserts equality. No new project, no PowerShell copy of the transformation.

Golden fixture: tests export 256 seeded points per function family (snoise float3/float2, snoise_grad, fbm_grad 4 octaves, ridged_grad, cellular, pcg3d/pcg4d, iv_* if present on main by then) with outputs as float32 bit patterns in hex, to tests/CultMath.Tests/fixtures/glsl-parity.json. JSON is tolerated here: the consumer is a browser-pane WebGL2 readback, a xenos boundary. The site cut evaluates it.

glslang: tools/get-glslang.ps1 fetches a pinned glslangValidator release the way tools/get-dxc.ps1 does; tools/compile-glsl.ps1 compiles a #version 300 es fragment wrapper that includes shaders/CultMath.glsl and calls every public function once. Run on Starfire, one job, detached with a log, polled in the foreground.

Verification on Yggdrasil: dotnet test from packages/cultmath/tests/CultMath.Tests; Stryker --since:c49c76ee from a plain clone (not a linked worktree: Stryker resolves --since paths against the main checkout). Never run verification as a background shell task.
keeps_moves: Both tracked CultMath.hlsl copies (packages/cultmath/shaders and unity/org.gamecult.cultmath/Shaders) stay one blob; the common-subset edits land in both.
The C# mirror test, the FXC probe and dxc -T lib_6_3 -HV 2021 all still pass on the edited HLSL; the Unity package does not ship the GLSL file.
design.md's HLSL -> C# transformation list (92-134) is unchanged; the GLSL list is a new sibling section.
adds: tests/CultMath.Tests/GlslLowering.cs: the HLSL -> GLSL ES 3.00 transformation, one static function string -> string, with the list as named steps in order: inline includes; drop guards and texture functions; type names; static const; casts via the balanced scanner; intrinsic renames (lerp, frac, saturate, rsqrt, asuint/asfloat); float literal passthrough; guards CULTMATH_GLSL added; a provenance header line naming the source file and that the file is generated.

tests/CultMath.Tests/GlslMirrorTests.cs: CommittedGlslEqualsLowering (writes when CULTMATH_WRITE_GLSL=1, prints a unified diff on failure); NoHlslOnlyTokensSurvive (regex over the output for float[234]\(|int[234]\(|lerp\(|frac\(|saturate\(|static const|\((float|int|uint)\)|Texture2D|SamplerState -> 0 matches); EveryPublicFunctionIsLowered (the set of cultmath_* function names in the HLSL minus the texture ones equals the set in the GLSL); GoldenFixtureMatchesCSharp (regenerates the fixture in memory from C# and asserts equality with the committed file).

tests/CultMath.Tests/fixtures/glsl-parity.json: the golden fixture (seed, points, per-function expected bit patterns, tolerance class per function: exact for integer-hash paths, ulp-bounded for transcendental).
tools/get-glslang.ps1 and tools/compile-glsl.ps1, mirroring get-dxc.ps1 / compile-hlsl-spirv.ps1 in shape.

packages/cultmath/docs/design.md: a section 'GLSL Target: Source Transformations' after :134 with the complete list, the common-subset rule for HLSL, the regeneration command, and that the GLSL is a derived file never edited by hand.

packages/cultmath/README.md: one paragraph that CultMath.glsl exists, what dialect it is, and how a WebGL consumer includes it (string concatenation before its own #version-led source; declare highp).

file_changes.change: step(h, 0.0) -> step(h, float4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)); same at :200. Bit-identical in HLSL and C#.
jitter components and the id at :502: an explicit (float) cast around the shifted uint before the float multiply, so the lowered text has no uint*float.
whatever common-subset edits the glslang compile demands; each one bit-identical, each one listed in the cut report.
new section: GLSL Target: Source Transformations.

authority_map.owner: GlslLowering (tests/CultMath.Tests) owns the HLSL -> GLSL transformation; shaders/CultMath.glsl is its derived output, pinned by GlslMirrorTests. CultMath.hlsl stays the one hand-written shader source.
inputs: C# math for the golden fixture values
outputs: shaders/CultMath.glsl (GLSL ES 3.00 library, every public cultmath_* function except texture samplers)
derived_state: CultMath.glsl is derived; a hand edit fails CommittedGlslEqualsLowering
the fixture is derived from C#; a stale fixture fails GoldenFixtureMatchesCSharp
forbidden_writers: no per-function special case in the lowering; a dialect gap is fixed in the HLSL in the common subset
no second transformation implementation (no PowerShell or JS copy of the rules)
no GLSL in the Unity package; no precision statement in the library file
shared_paths: both tracked CultMath.hlsl copies receive the same edits; the existing one-blob rule covers them
the same dotnet test run pins the C# mirror, the GLSL pin and the fixture
authority_map.deletion_line: Nothing is deleted in CultLib. The liability bought is one generated file, one test file, one fixture and two tool scripts; what it retires is every future hand copy of CultMath noise in a GLSL consumer, starting with the site.
